problem: Frame-based visual controllers for human-following robots run at fixed rates and suffer from motion blur and latency; event cameras have rarely been combined with RL for human-robot navigation, and pure RL from scratch is sample-inefficient.
motivation: Event cameras offer microsecond resolution, high dynamic range and minimal motion blur, and their asynchrony permits adaptive inference and control rates. Human-centered social robots need reliable person following with obstacle avoidance, and hybrid IL+RL training could cut RL learning time.
key_idea: Combine an event-camera YOLOv5s pedestrian detector (SAE representation) with depth and LIDAR in a state fed to a DDPG controller whose actor is initialized by behavior cloning of a PD controller.
insight: The RL controller (DDPG initialized from IL) tracks the target more closely than PD or IL alone: mean x_box 171.2 px vs the 173 px target (PD 167.1, IL 172.2) with lower std (27.4 vs 46.9 for PD), and mean distance 2.08 m vs the 2 m target (PD 2.59). The IL warm start yields a workable policy quickly. There is no ablation of training time, and RL has higher linear-velocity variance (SD 0.24), so the gains are modest and simulation-only.
method: Sensors: Pioneer 3-AT with DAVIS346 event camera, RealSense depth (via homography from event to RGB-D frame) and a 2D Hokuyo LIDAR for obstacles within 0.5 m
Event pedestrian detector: YOLOv5s trained on PEDRo with SAE representation and a 10 ms accumulation window; provides the bounding box x-center
PD expert controller: PD on bbox position (target x=173, y=140), depth distance and LIDAR generates expert trajectories
Imitation learning: behavior cloning with an MSE loss trains a 30-30 MLP actor from successful PD trajectories
DDPG refinement: 6-D state [v, w, x_box, d_ped, d_obs, theta_obs], actions are velocity increments every 0.1 s, actor initialized from IL, OU noise, replay buffer

Reward: +500 when centered (<1 px) and at distance (<0.1 m error); -500 on collision or losing the person (d>3 m or d<1 m); otherwise a quadratic penalty on distance and centering errors with a coupling factor alpha
Simulation: Gazebo/ROS 21x12 m scenario, pedestrian at 0.7 m/s on a figure-eight path over 100 s, with termination conditions

setting.backbone: YOLOv5s (event detector, trained) + DDPG actor-critic MLPs 6-30-30-2 (IL-initialized, trained from scratch otherwise)
setting.training_data: PEDRo event dataset (119 recordings, 43,259 boxes, 27k samples) for detection; a few PD expert trajectories for IL; online RL in Gazebo
setting.observation: event camera (SAE image) bbox + RealSense depth distance + 2D LIDAR nearest obstacle + robot velocities
setting.action_space: continuous velocity increments (dv in [-0.2,0.2], dw in [-0.5,0.5]) every 0.1 s

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark; only controller statistics (mean/std of velocity, x_box, d_ped) in Table 1 and figures for a custom Gazebo person-following scenario.
results: In simulation, the RL controller follows the pedestrian best: x_box mean 171.2376 px (target 173), d_ped mean 2.0756 m (target 2 m), std of x_box 27.4392 vs PD 46.9139. IL is comparable in mean (172.2215 px, 2.0846 m) but with a larger x_box std (34.3104); PD is worst (167.0698 px, 2.5889 m).
limitations: Simulation only with a single scenario and trajectory; no real-robot tests and no standard benchmarks or success metrics
Still depends on RGB-D and LIDAR in addition to the event camera; claimed reduction in RL training time is not quantified
Comparison is only descriptive statistics; RL has higher linear-velocity variance and no ablation or multiple seeds
